What does that mean?

Terms, in plain language.

The words you come across when it is about AI and findability. Explained briefly, with a link if you want to read more.

AEO

Answer Engine Optimization. Another name for roughly the same as GEO: making sure your content can be used as an answer.

Read more →

AI Overview

The written answer Google shows above the ordinary results for some searches, with links to the sources.

Read more →

AI visibility

How often and how well a company is mentioned in the answers of AI systems such as ChatGPT and Gemini. You measure it by asking real customer questions and counting in how many answers you appear.

Read more →

Baseline check

A first measurement of where you stand now, before you change anything. At NXEO: for which buying questions ChatGPT mentions your company and who appears instead.

Read more →

Buying question

A question from someone looking for a company, such as "who can do this for me" or "what does it cost". These are the questions you want to be mentioned for.

Read more →

Crawler

A program that visits and reads websites. Search engines and AI companies each have their own crawlers.

GEO

Generative Engine Optimization. The work you do to be mentioned in an answer written by an AI system. Most of it overlaps with ordinary SEO.

Read more →

Google Business Profile

Your free listing in Google Search and Maps, with address, opening hours, services and reviews. Gemini leans on it heavily for local questions.

Read more →

GPTBot

OpenAI's crawler that collects text to train models. It is a different one from the crawler for search.

Hallucination

An AI system says something that is not true, with the same confidence as something that is. About companies an error usually comes from an outdated or wrong source.

Read more →

Index

The collection of pages a search engine knows. If you are not in it, that search engine cannot show you, and neither can an AI system that leans on it.

Read more →

Language model

The software behind an AI system. It was trained on a very large amount of text and writes new text based on that. Often shortened to LLM.

Live search

An AI system searches the internet while answering and uses what it finds. New pages can therefore show up in answers within weeks.

Read more →

llms.txt

A proposal for a file that gives AI systems a summary of your website. It is not a standard, and it has not been shown that the major systems use it. Do not expect miracles from it.

Mention

Your company name appears in the answer. That can be with or without a link, and with a right or a wrong description.

Read more →

OAI-SearchBot

OpenAI's crawler for the search feature of ChatGPT. If you block it, ChatGPT cannot show your pages as a source.

Read more →

Presence score

The figure from 0 to 100 with which NXEO sums up for customers how often and how well they are mentioned, across several AI systems.

Read more →

Prompt

The question or instruction someone gives an AI system. For a company the prompts of customers are the starting point.

Read more →

robots.txt

A small file on your website that says which crawlers may read which pages. A mistake here can make you invisible without you noticing.

Read more →

SEO

Search Engine Optimization. The work you do to rank high in the ordinary Google search results. A good basis here also helps with AI.

Read more →

Source or citation

The page an AI system takes part of its answer from, often with a link. Being mentioned and being used as a source are two different things.

Read more →

Structured data

Extra code in a page that says in a fixed form what is on it: a company, a question with an answer, a price. It helps search engines understand your content.

Training data

The texts a language model was trained on. What they said about your company is inside the model itself and only changes with a new version.

Read more →
